title: AP-LS Conference Website Guide
text:
Welcome
This guide is for the co-chairs of the annual AP-LS conference. It explains how the conference pages on ap-ls.org are put together and how to keep them current through your conference year.
You do not need to know R or Quarto for routine updates. The conference pages are plain text files with some structure around them. If you can edit a document and rename a file, you can handle most of the work in this guide.

title: AP-LS Conference Website Guide
text:
What this guide covers

How the conference pages fit together and where each file lives
What to update at each point in the conference year
How to open the call for proposals and add preconference workshops
How to hand the site over to the next year’s co-chairs

It covers the mechanics only. Decisions about content, such as deadlines, rates, and the theme of the call for proposals, stay with you and the conference committee.

title: AP-LS Conference Website Guide
text:
The two reference documents
Two files in the website folder carry the full detail. This guide points to them instead of repeating them:

UPDATING.md in the project root covers setup, previewing, images, and how changes reach the live site.
conferences/_template/README.md is the checklist for starting a new conference year.

When this guide and those files ever disagree, trust the files. They are updated every time the site changes.

title: 1  Getting started
text:
1.1 What you need
The full setup walkthrough, including how to get a copy of the site and the one-time install steps, is in UPDATING.md under “Getting a copy of the website” and “One-time setup”.

title: 1  Getting started
text:
A copy of the website folder. Ask the web editor for the current version. Keep it somewhere stable on your computer and treat it as the single place where edits happen.
Quarto. The free download from quarto.org is all you need to preview and render pages.
A text editor. RStudio is the easiest option because it has a Render button and a “Replace in Files” tool that the yearly setup relies on. VS Code works too. You do not need to write any R code for routine updates.

title: 1  Getting started
text:
1.2 Previewing your work
From the project root (the folder that contains _quarto.yml), run:
quarto preview
This opens the site in your browser and refreshes it as you save files. To build a single page instead:
quarto render conferences/index.qmd
Rendered pages land in the docs/ folder. That folder is what eventually goes live, so a quick look at your page in the browser is the best check before you hand anything off.

title: 1  Getting started
text:
1.3 When you are finished editing
You never publish directly. When your changes look right in the preview, share the changed files with the web editor, keeping their folder structure intact. The exact handoff steps are in UPDATING.md under “How changes reach the live site”. Nothing you do in your local copy can break the live site, so experiment freely.

title: 2  How the conference pages fit together
text:
2.1 The main page is the hub
Everything for the conference lives in the conferences/ folder of the website project:
conferences/index.qmd is what visitors see when they choose your conference from the site’s Conferences menu. Near the top it has a grid of icon tiles linking to each section and to the two sub-pages. The sections on the page are: General Information, Submissions, Hotel Information, Schedule, Registration, and Preconference Workshops.
crumbs: 2  How the conference pages fit together

title: 2  How the conference pages fit together
section: 2.2 The Google Sheet and the data folder
text:
2.2 The Google Sheet and the data folder
Facts that change during the year (announcement notes, deadlines, booking and registration links, rates, and the workshop list) live in the AP-LS Conference Google Sheet. Running conferences/_update-conference.R copies them into conferences/data/ and builds the workshop pages. The pages read those local files when they render, so the published site never depends on Google being reachable.
crumbs: 2  How the conference pages fit together

title: 2  How the conference pages fit together
text:
2.3 The sub-pages
Two topics get their own pages so they can grow through the year without crowding the main page:

cfp/index.qmd holds the call for proposals.
preconference/index.qmd lists the workshops and their prices. The listing grid builds itself from the workshop folders, which the update script creates from the Sheet.
crumbs: 2  How the conference pages fit together

title: 2  How the conference pages fit together
text:
2.4 Archive and template
archive/ holds one folder per past year, including that year’s data/ folder, so archived pages stay frozen in time. When your conference ends, your pages move there and the next year starts from conferences/_template/. The underscore in the name keeps the template out of the published site.
crumbs: 2  How the conference pages fit together

title: 2  How the conference pages fit together
text:
2.5 Things you rarely touch

index.css controls the look of the conference pages. Change it only if the web editor asks you to.
The R code chunks in the pages move Sheet values onto the page. They are machinery; edit the Sheet instead.
crumbs: 2  How the conference pages fit together

title: 3  The conference year, stage by stage
text:
3.1 The five stages
The conference pages are built to go up before all the details are known. Everything that changes during the year lives in the AP-LS Conference Google Sheet, so most updates never touch the website files at all.
The update loop is always the same:
crumbs: 3  The conference year, stage by stage

title: 3  The conference year, stage by stage
text:
3.2 What the Sheet controls

The announcement note in each section of the main page
The CFP announcement, deadline, portal link, and reviewer form link
The room-block note and booking link (and whether the callout shows)
The registration note and link (and whether the Register button shows)
Registration and workshop rates tables
The workshop pages themselves, one row per workshop
crumbs: 3  The conference year, stage by stage

title: 3  The conference year, stage by stage
section: 3.3 What still lives in the page files
text:
3.3 What still lives in the page files
The yearly facts (year, city, dates, hotel name and address), the photos, the section headings, and the full text of the call for proposals. Those change once a year at most, and the yearly setup chapter covers them.
The pages read local copies of the Sheet data, committed alongside the site. Visitors always see the last rendered version, and the site builds fine even when Google Drive is unreachable.
crumbs: 3  The conference year, stage by stage

title: 4  Common updates
text:
4.1 Open the call for proposals
Nearly every update during the conference year takes one command, run from the project root:
This pulls the Sheet into the local files, renders the whole site, and runs the accessibility and link checks. At the end it tells you whether everything passed. If a check finds something, the script prints what and where so you can fix it before committing. The link check always finds a handful of references buried in the archived email newsletters; those are expected, and the script says so when that is all it found.
The update script copies the Sheet into local files the pages read, so what you see after rendering is exactly what the Sheet says. The Sheet’s tabs and columns are listed in the comment at the top of conferences/_update-conference.R.
When you only want to preview a small change, the manual three-step routine still works:

title: 4  Common updates
text:
In the info tab, set submissions_note (the line on the main page), cfp_note (the line on the CFP page), cfp_deadline, submission_portal_url, and reviewer_form_url.
Run the update script.
Open conferences/cfp/index.qmd and follow the STAGE 2 comment at the top: delete the comment markers so the full call becomes visible, add this year’s theme, and check the session limits against this year’s policy. The deadline and links fill in from the Sheet on their own.
Render conferences/cfp/index.qmd and conferences/index.qmd.

title: 4  Common updates
text:
4.2 Add a preconference workshop

Add one row to the workshops tab: slug (a folder name like workshop_1), title, subtitle, date, presenters, categories, description, learning objectives, CE credits, and times. Separate multiple presenters or objectives with semicolons.
Run the update script. It builds a page for each workshop in conferences/preconference/, and the workshops grid fills in on its own.
When the first workshop goes up, set sort-ui and filter-ui to true in conferences/preconference/index.qmd.
Render conferences/preconference/.

Workshops can go up one at a time as they are confirmed. To remove one, delete its row from the Sheet, re-run the script, and delete its folder (the script warns about folders that are not in the Sheet and leaves them untouched).

title: 4  Common updates
text:
4.3 Open the room block
In the info tab, set hotel_note (for example, “The 20XX room block is now available! Book directly through the hotel for the discounted rate.”) and hotel_booking_url. Run the script and render the main page. The booking callout with the Book Room button appears on its own.

title: 4  Common updates
text:
4.4 Update the schedule
Set schedule_note in the info tab, then run the script and render the main page. If the program is a PDF, keep it in conferences/files/ and link it from the Schedule section of conferences/index.qmd.

title: 4  Common updates
text:
4.5 Open registration

In the info tab, set registration_note and registration_url.
Put the final prices in the registration-rates tab, and the workshop prices in the workshop-rates tab. Keep rates_note accurate: it says which year the rates are based on until the new rates are set.
Run the script and render the main page and the preconference page. The Register button appears on its own.

title: 4  Common updates
text:
4.6 Add images
Save conference images in conferences/images/ and resize and compress them before adding. Large images are the main reason pages load slowly. The naming and size rules are in UPDATING.md under “Image guidelines”.

title: 5  Starting a new conference year
text:
5.1 The steps
Once a year, after the conference wraps up, the site moves to the next year. The checklist of record is conferences/_template/README.md. This chapter is the overview so you know what the steps are for.
crumbs: 5  Starting a new conference year

title: 5  Starting a new conference year
text:
Archive the year that ended. Move the live files (conferences/index.qmd, index.css, images/, data/, cfp/, and preconference/) into conferences/archive/ under the year that just ended. Then open the archived index.qmd and change its two archive links (the Archives tile and the Learn More button) to ../index.qmd so they lead back to the new current page. The archived pages keep reading their own year’s data/ folder, so they stay frozen in time.
Copy the template. Copy everything in conferences/_template/ up into conferences/. Copy, do not move, so the template stays clean for the following year.
Replace the placeholders. The comment at the top of the new index.qmd lists every placeholder: the year, city, dates, and hotel. “Replace in Files” in RStudio or VS Code handles each one in a single pass. The same placeholders appear in the seed CSVs in data/, so run the replacements there too.
Add the images. Save the new conference logo as images/logo.png and a hotel photo as images/hotel.png in conferences/images/.
Set up the Google Sheet. Hand the conference Sheet to the new co-chairs (or make next year’s copy with the structure documented in conferences/_update-conference.R), then run source("conferences/_update-conference.R") to pull it into the site.
crumbs: 5  Starting a new conference year

title: 5  Starting a new conference year
section: 5.2 One step outside the conference folder
text:
5.2 One step outside the conference folder
The Conferences menu in the site navbar names the current year. After the rollover, open _quarto.yml in the project root, find the Conferences menu, and update the label to the new year. The link itself does not change; only the label does.
crumbs: 5  Starting a new conference year

title: 5  Starting a new conference year
text:
5.3 Then render and hand off
Render the conference pages and check them in the browser: the main page, cfp/index.qmd, and preconference/index.qmd. When they look right, share the changed files with the web editor as described in UPDATING.md.
The new page works immediately after step 3, with “coming soon” notes everywhere. The rest of the year runs through the Google Sheet, as the previous chapter describes.
crumbs: 5  Starting a new conference year

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
6.1 Before the season
The whole year on one page. Details for each item are in the earlier chapters. “Update the Sheet” always means: edit the conference Google Sheet, run source("conferences/_update-conference.R"), then render the conference pages.

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
Get a copy of the website folder from the web editor
Install Quarto, R, and RStudio
Preview the site locally once, so you know the tooling works
Make sure you can edit the conference Google Sheet

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
6.2 After the previous conference (rollover)

Archive the old year into conferences/archive/ (include data/)
Copy conferences/_template/ into conferences/
Replace every placeholder, in the pages and in data/*.csv
Add images/logo.png and images/hotel.png
Update the year in the Conferences menu in _quarto.yml
Update the Sheet for the new year and run the update script
Render the conference pages and hand off to the web editor

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
6.3 Fall

Set the CFP keys in the Sheet, then open up the full call in cfp/index.qmd (Stage 2)
Add workshop rows to the Sheet as workshops are confirmed
Set sort-ui and filter-ui on the preconference page once the first workshop is up
Set hotel_note and hotel_booking_url when the room block opens (Stage 3)

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
6.4 Winter

Set schedule_note when the program is ready (Stage 4)
Set registration_note and registration_url, and fill in the rates tabs (Stage 5)

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
6.5 After your conference

Send the web editor any final program PDFs for the archive
Hand the website folder, the Google Sheet, this guide, and your notes to next year’s co-chairs

title: 6  Season checklist
text:
6.6 Where to get help

Mechanics of editing and previewing: UPDATING.md in the project root
The yearly rollover: conferences/_template/README.md
The Sheet structure: header comments of conferences/_update-conference.R
Anything stuck or broken: the web editor, webeditor@ap-ls.org
